newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom to pay 3 bln DM div.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom to pay 3 bln DM div.

text.p: German telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom AG, at a news conference ahead of its planned share market listing, said on Friday it would pay a dividend of three billion marks on its 1997 earnings, or about 1.20 marks per share.
The Telekom IPO is planned for 500 million shares with a face value of five marks, but Telekom said it could offer banks a green-shoe offer of up to an additional 75 million shares.
Shares in the company will total 2.53 billion.
Telekom said it planned to reduce its debt to 65 billion marks by the year 2000 from 107 billion marks now.
The subscription period for the share offering will be October 22 to November 14.
Chief financial officer Joachim Kroeske said the dividend for 1996 would total about 1.5 billion marks ($980.3 million). The new Telekom shares will be eligible for the full 1996 dividend, he said.
Telekom's 107 billion mark debt is already down 20 billion marks from January 1995, Kroeske said.
Banks' greenshoe option for the additional 75 million shares is limited to 30 days, he said.

Telekom will specify a price range for the new shares at the beginning of the subscription period, and will set the final offering price on November 16 or 17. Listing in Frankfurt and New York is set for November 18, and in Tokyo for November 19.
